To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an accurate model to study in real time the evolution of the refractive index profile in photopolymiers and we have demonstrated the importance of the spatial frequency in the material volume variations.
we have studied the influence on the spatial frequency on phase and surface profile evolution of the gratings and we have proposed an experimental method to calculate the diffusion coefficient.

we have demonstrated the influence in dark of the monomer diffusion in the range of spatial frequency between 2 and 6 lines per mm in PVA/AA photopolymer, and we have obtained a method to estimate the diffusivity of monomers inside photopolymeric materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method to study the in dark evolution of the gratings and the monomer diffusion in PVA/AA photopolymers.
the development of a new method to evaluate monomer diffusivities in holographic materials.
the development of a new method for the study of diffusion effects in holographic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the monomer diffusion is an important phenomenon in the photopolymerization process.
the monomer diffusion in photopolymiers is an effect that must be taken into account to achieve a high diffraction efficiency.
the evolution of the phase modulation is not a simple linear evolution, and the diffusion effects are more complex than previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the in dark evolution of the gratings is an important factor to take into account in the analysis of photopolymers at low spatial frequencies, and the monomer diffusions can be estimated from the in dark evolution.
the in dark evolution of the grater profile must be taken into account for low spatial frequencies, in order to obtain the maximum diffraction efficiency.
we have studied the evolution of phase modulation in dark and in dark and under UV illumination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the monomer diffusive coefficient can be estimated using a simple method based on the evolution of the diffraction efficiency of a holographic grating.
it is possible, by using low spatial frequencies, to evaluate the monomer diffusion in real time.
we have shown the influence of the diffusion on the grating profile and the possibility to obtain a diffraction efficiency of 35% in the first order.
